education.classification_note: FRAC and IRAC are separate systems. Codes describe resistance-management groups, not safety, efficacy, or approved uses. Unmapped ingredients remain unclassified; this does not mean they have no group or no resistance risk. Biological strain and plant-incorporated protectant assignments require separate review.
education.resistance_note: Changing brands does not necessarily change the mode of action. Count only components effective against the target pest. Mixtures do not replace a resistance-management plan. Follow label restrictions and crop-specific Extension guidance across seed, soil, and foliar uses.
education.technology_note: Biological describes an origin or technology and can overlap with fungicide, insecticide, or nematicide functions. Plant-incorporated protectants (PIPs) are produced within the plant; they are not seed coatings. The EPA site census can also include fumigants and other technologies; inclusion is not a recommendation to apply them as a seed coating.
education.signal_note: Signal words describe acute hazard of the formulated pesticide as sold. They do not rank efficacy or summarize chronic or environmental risks. Do not infer POISON or a skull-and-crossbones from DANGER alone. EPA workbook values are not a review of the current label; an SDS signal word is not a substitute for the EPA label signal word.
education.data_note: Product signal words and restricted-use flags come only from that registration's EPA workbook row. Blank distributor fields are not filled from a base product. "None" reported by EPA and missing data remain distinct. Exact PPE, first aid, environmental hazards, planting restrictions, and disposal instructions must be checked on the current label and seed tag.

treatments.purpose: Protect seed and seedlings from specified seedborne or soilborne pathogens.
treatments.compare: Compare labeled pathogens, ingredients, and FRAC groups.
treatments.limit: Protection varies by pathogen; no single ingredient covers every seedling disease.

treatments.purpose: Manage specified insects during crop establishment.
treatments.compare: Use pest history and crop-specific IPM guidance; compare IRAC groups.
treatments.limit: Benefits depend on pest pressure. Early protection does not imply season-long control.

treatments.purpose: Reduce early root exposure to specified plant-parasitic nematodes.
treatments.compare: Use nematode testing and labeled species claims.
treatments.limit: Combine with resistant varieties and rotation; seed treatment alone may be inadequate.

treatments.purpose: Use a microorganism or qualifying natural substance to manage a labeled pest.
treatments.compare: Check the exact strain or substance and target pest.
treatments.limit: The biological category can overlap with the functions above; follow its label.

treatments.purpose: Support legume nodulation and biological nitrogen fixation.
treatments.compare: Check crop compatibility and field history.
treatments.limit: An inoculant is not automatically a pesticide. Verify compatibility with other seed-applied products.

signals.meaning: Highest acute toxicity category I in at least one assessed endpoint.
signals.note: POISON / skull-and-crossbones depends on the basis for category I; consult the label.
Read the hazard statements, PPE, and first-aid directions.

signals.meaning: Category III; may also be used voluntarily for category IV.
signals.note: Does not mean harmless or suitable for every use.
Category IV does not require a signal word, but do not infer a product's category from this field alone.

signals.meaning: The export field is blank, absent, or unrecognized.
signals.note: Unknown is not equivalent to no hazard. Check that registration's label.

bmps.title: Start with a pest-management need
bmps.text: Use crop and field history, scouting or diagnostic tests, and local Extension guidance to choose components for the target problem.

bmps.title: Check the current label and seed tag
bmps.text: Verify crop, target pest, rates, application method, PPE, worker protections, planting restrictions, and first aid. Follow applicable restricted-use requirements.

bmps.title: Control abrasion and dust
bmps.text: Handle bags gently; maintain planting equipment. Use seed-flow lubricants and equipment settings permitted by the label and manufacturer.

bmps.title: Protect pollinators and water
bmps.text: Consider flowering areas, bee activity, wind, and nearby water. Avoid loading or cleaning where dust can reach bees; follow label precautions.

bmps.title: Clean up and keep seed segregated
bmps.text: Promptly address spilled seed and dust as directed. Keep treated seed out of food, feed, and oil channels. Follow label storage and disposal directions.

bmps.title: Plan for resistance and compatibility
bmps.text: Review FRAC/IRAC groups across the crop program. Check compatibility and storage instructions for each component, including inoculants. Keep product and treatment records.

records.targets: Soybean sudden death syndrome, early-season Septoria brown spot, charcoal rot; cyst, root-knot, reniform, lesion and lance nematodes.
records.rate: Soybeans: 1.52–3.04 fl oz product/100 lb seed, or 0.714–1.428 fl oz/140,000 seeds (weight conversion assumes 3,000 seeds/lb).
records.application: Water-based slurry with commercial seed-treatment equipment; on-farm use is subject to crop restrictions. No hopper-box, planter-box or slurry-box application at planting.
records.rei: 12 hours; a soil-incorporated-seed exception has WPS conditions.
records.ppe: Long sleeves, long pants, shoes/socks and label-specified chemical-resistant gloves; see section 2.2 for materials and requirements.
records.restrictions: Soybean section carries a California registration qualification. No soybean hay, forage or silage use. Annual pydiflumetofen limit: 0.357 lb ai/acre across seed and foliar uses. Consult the full label.

records.targets: Soybeans: labeled control of listed Rhizoctonia, Fusarium and Phytophthora seedling diseases, seed-borne Phomopsis, and Aspergillus/Penicillium seed rot. Pythium is listed for suppression.
records.rate: Soybeans: 0.25 fl oz product/140,000 seeds (0.50 fl oz/100 lb at 2,800 seeds/lb).
records.application: Commercial facilities or mobile treaters using closed transfer, mixing/loading, calibration and treatment. No hopper-box, planter-box or slurry-box use.
records.rei: 12 hours; consult the agricultural-use requirements and applicable exceptions.
records.ppe: See full label; handler PPE not transcribed into this extract.
records.restrictions: Add an approved colorant. Treated seed is not for food, feed or oil. Follow bag-label requirements. No subsequent foliar/soil OSBP-inhibitor application following this seed treatment; consult complete resistance directions.
